GFDD.SM.01.note: Stock price volatility is the average of the 360-day volatility of the national stock market index.

GFDD.OM.02.note: Stock market return is the growth rate of annual average stock market index. Annual average stock market index is constructed by taking the average of the daily stock market indexes available at Bloomberg.

GFDD.OM.01.nameEn: Number of listed companies per 1,000,000 people
GFDD.OM.01.note: Number of publicly listed companies per 1,000,000 people. Number of listed domestic companies is the domestically incorporated companies listed on the country's stock exchanges at the end of the year. This indicator does not include investment companies, mutual funds, or other collective investment vehicles.
GFDD.OM.01.org: Global Stock Markets Factbook and supplemental S&P data, Standard & Poor's

GFDD.EM.01.note: Ratio of the value of total shares traded to average real market capitalization, the denominator is deflated using the following method:  Tt/P_at/{(0.5)*[Mt/P_et + Mt-1/P_et-1] where T is total value traded, M is stock market capitalization, P_e is end-of period CPI. (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF) and annual CPI (IFS line 64..ZF) are from the IMF’s International Financial Statistics.
GFDD.EM.01.org: Global Stock Markets Factbook and supplemental S&P data, Standard & Poor's

GFDD.DM.12.nameEn: Syndicated loan issuance volume to GDP (%)

GFDD.DM.02.nameEn: Stock market total value traded to GDP (%)
GFDD.DM.02.note: Total value of all traded shares in a stock market exchange as a percentage of GDP.  Following deflation method is use:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is stock market capitalization, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a  is average annual CPI. End-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF) and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DM.02.org: Global Stock Markets Factbook and supplemental S&P data, Standard & Poor's

GFDD.DM.01.note: Value of listed shares to GDP, calculated using the following deflation  method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is stock market capitalization, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a  is average annual CPI. End-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF) and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DM.01.org: Global Stock Markets Factbook and supplemental S&P data, Standard & Poor's

GFDD.DM.06.nameEn: Outstanding international public debt securities to GDP (%)
GFDD.DM.06.note: Amount of public international debt securities (amounts outstanding), as a share of GDP. It covers long-term bonds and notes and money market instruments placed on international markets. Table 12D (international debt amount): governments / GDP. End of year data (i.e. December data) are considered for debt securities. The figures are deflated using the following methodology: {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is the level international public debt, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. GDP is from World Development Indicators. End-of period CPI is taken from IFS line 64M..ZF month of December (or if not available Q4). Average annual CPI is constructed from the monthly CPI figure taken from IFS line 64..ZF.

GFDD.DM.05.nameEn: Outstanding international private debt securities to GDP (%)
GFDD.DM.05.note: Amount of private international debt securities (amounts outstanding), as a share of GDP. It covers long-term bonds and notes and money market instruments placed on international markets. (Table 12A  (international debt amount: all issuers) - Table 12D (international debt amount: governments)) / GDP. End of year data (i.e. December data) are considered for debt securities. The figures are deflated using the following methodology: {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is the level intenational private debt, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. GDP is from World Development Indicators.End-of period CPI is taken from IFS line 64M..ZF month of December (or if not available Q4). Average annual CPI is constructed from the monthly CPI figure taken from IFS line 64..ZF.

GFDD.DM.07.note: Total value of outstanding international debt issues both public and private, as a share of GDP. Offshore bank loan data from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 12A (Amount Outstanding): International debt securities - all issuers.

GFDD.DM.16.nameEn: Credit flows by fintech and bigtech companies to GDP (%)

GFDD.DM.13.nameEn: Corporate bond issuance volume to GDP (%)

GFDD.AM.01.nameEn: Value traded excluding top 10 traded companies to total value traded (%)
GFDD.AM.01.note: Value of all traded shares outside of the top ten largest traded companies as a share of total value of all traded shares in a stock market exchange. WFE provides data on the exchange level. This variable is aggregated up to the country level by taking a simple average over exchanges.

GFDD.AM.02.nameEn: Market capitalization excluding top 10 companies to total market capitalization (%)
GFDD.AM.02.note: Value of listed shares outside of the top ten largest companies to total value of all listed shares.

GFDD.SI.07.note: Provisions to nonperforming loans. Nonperforming Loans are loans for which the contractual payments are delinquent, usually defined as and NPL ratio  being overdue for more than a certain number of days (e.g., usually more than 90 days). Reported by IMF staff. Note that due to differences in national accounting, taxation, and supervisory regimes, these data are not strictly comparable across countries.
GFDD.SI.07.org: Financial Soundness Indicators Database (fsi.imf.org), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.SI.06.nameEn: Liquid assets to deposits and short term funding (%)
GFDD.SI.06.note: Raw data are from Bankscope.  Data2075 / data2030. Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.SI.01.note: It captures the probability of default of a country's banking system. Z-score compares the buffer of a country's banking system (capitalization and returns) with the volatility of those returns. It is estimated as (ROA+(equity/assets))/sd(ROA); sd(ROA) is the standard deviation of ROA. ROA, equity, and assets are country-level aggregate figures Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.SI.05.nameEn: Bank regulatory capital to risk-weighted assets (%)
GFDD.SI.05.note: Reported by IMF staff. Note that due to differences in national accounting, taxation, and supervisory regimes, these data are not strictly comparable across countries.
GFDD.SI.05.org: Financial Soundness Indicators Database (fsi.imf.org), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.SI.02.nameEn: Bank non-performing loans to gross loans (%)
GFDD.SI.02.note: Reported by IMF staff. Note that due to differences in national accounting, taxation, and supervisory regimes, these data are not strictly comparable across countries.
GFDD.SI.02.org: Financial Soundness Indicators Database (fsi.imf.org), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.SI.04.note: Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Private credit by deposit money banks (IFS line 22d); bank deposits (IFS lines 24 and 25).
GFDD.SI.04.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.SI.03.note: Ratio of bank capital and reserves to total assets. Capital and reserves include funds contributed by owners, retained earnings, general and special reserves, provisions, and valuation adjustments. Capital includes tier 1 capital (paid-up shares and common stock), which is a common feature in all countries' banking systems, and total regulatory capital, which includes several specified types of subordinated debt instruments that need not be repaid if the funds are required to maintain minimum capital levels (these comprise tier 2 and tier 3 capital). Total assets include all nonfinancial and financial assets. Reported by IMF staff. Note that due to differences in national accounting, taxation, and supervisory regimes, these data are not strictly comparable across countries.
GFDD.SI.03.org: Financial Soundness Indicators Database (fsi.imf.org), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.OI.18.note: GDP data provided by IFS and converted into USD using IFS exchange rates.

GFDD.OI.13.note: Workers' remittances and compensation of employees comprise current transfers by migrant workers and wages and salaries earned by nonresident workers. Data are the sum of three items defined in the fifth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: workers' remittances, compensation of employees, and migrants' transfers. Remittances are classified as current private transfers from migrant workers resident in the host country for more than a year, irrespective of their immigration status, to recipients in their country of origin. Migrants' transfers are defined as the net worth of migrants who are expected to remain in the host country for more than one year that is transferred from one country to another at the time of migration. Compensation of employees is the income of migrants who have lived in the host country for less than a year.

GFDD.OI.08.nameEn: Loans from nonresident banks (net) to GDP (%)
GFDD.OI.08.note: Ratio of net offshore bank loans to GDP. An offshore bank is a bank located outside the country of residence of the depositor, typically in a low tax jurisdiction (or tax haven) that provides financial and legal advantages. Offshore bank loan data from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 12A (Net Issues): International debt securities - all issuers.

GFDD.OI.09.nameEn: Loans from nonresident banks (amounts outstanding) to GDP (%)
GFDD.OI.09.note: Ratio of outstanding offshore bank loans to GDP. An offshore bank is a bank located outside the country of residence of the depositor, typically in a low tax jurisdiction (or tax haven) that provides financial and legal advantages. Offshore bank loan data from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 7A: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis all sectors.

GFDD.OI.07.nameEn: Liquid liabilities in millions USD (2000 constant)
GFDD.OI.07.note: Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF's International Financial Statistics. Liquid liabilities (IFS lines 55L..ZF or, if not available, line 35L..ZF); for Eurocurrency area countries (BEF, DEM, ESP, FRF, GRD, IEP, ITL, LUF, NLG, ATS, PTE, FIM), liquid liabilities are estimated by summing IFS items 34A, 34B and 35.
GFDD.OI.07.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.OI.20a.nameEn: Government bank assets among total bank assets (%)

GFDD.OI.15.note: Percentage of the number of foreign owned banks to the number of the total banks in an Economy. A foreign bank is a bank where 50 percent or more of its shares are owned by foreigners.
GFDD.OI.15.org: Stijn Claessens and Neeltje van Horen, 2012. "Foreign Banks: Trends, Impact and Financial Stability" IMF Working Paper, WP/12/10

GFDD.OI.16a.nameEn: Foreign bank assets among total banks assets (%)

GFDD.OI.16.nameEn: Foreign bank assets among total bank assets (%)
GFDD.OI.16.note: Percentage of the total banking assets that are held by foreign banks. A foreign bank is a bank where 50 percent or more of its shares are owned by foreigners.
GFDD.OI.16.org: Stijn Claessens and Neeltje van Horen, 2012. "Foreign Banks: Trends, Impact and Financial Stability" IMF Working Paper, WP/12/10

GFDD.OI.11.nameEn: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis the nonbanking sectors (% of domestic bank deposits)
GFDD.OI.11.note: Data is from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 7B: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis nonbanking sectors; bank deposits from IFS (IFS lines 24 and 25). End of year data (i.e. December data) are used.

GFDD.OI.10.nameEn: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis the banking sector (% of domestic bank deposits)
GFDD.OI.10.note: Data is from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 7A minus 7B: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis all sectors minus external loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis nonbanking sectors; bank deposits from IFS (IFS lines 24 and 25). End of year data (i.e. December data) are used.

GFDD.OI.12.nameEn: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis all sectors (% of domestic bank deposits)
GFDD.OI.12.note: Data is from BIS Statistical Appendix Table 7A: External loans and deposits of reporting banks vis-à-vis all sectors; bank deposits from IFS (IFS lines 24 and 25). End of year data (i.e. December data) are used.

GFDD.OI.14.nameEn: Consolidated foreign claims of BIS reporting banks to GDP (%)
GFDD.OI.14.note: The ratio of consolidated foreign claims to GDP of the banks that are reporting to BIS. Foreign claims are defined as the sum of cross-border claims plus foreign offices’ local claims in all currencies. In the consolidated banking statistics claims that are granted or extended to nonresidents are referred to as either cross-border claims.  In the context of the consolidated banking statistics, local claims refer to claims of domestic banks’ foreign affiliates (branches/subsidiaries) on the residents of the host country (i.e. country of residence of affiliates). Items (A+L from BIS Table 9A). End-of-year data (i.e. December data) are considered for banks claims. GDP is from World Development Indicators.
GFDD.OI.14.org: Consolidated banking statistics, Bank for International Settlements (BIS)

GFDD.OI.19.note: A banking crisis is defined as systemic if two conditions are met: a. Significant signs of financial distress in the banking system (as indicated bysignificant bank runs, losses in the banking system, and/or bank liquidations), b. Significant banking policy intervention measures in response to significant losses in the banking system. The first year that both criteria are met is considered as the year when the crisis start becoming systemic.  The end of a crisis is defined the year before both real GDP growth and real credit growth are positive for at least two consecutive years.
GFDD.OI.19.org: Luc Laeven and Fabián Valencia, 2012. “Systemic Banking Crises Database: An Update”, IMF Working Paper WP/12/163

GFDD.OI.02.note: Demand, time and saving deposits in deposit money banks as a share of GDP, calculated using the following deflation method: {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is demand and time and saving deposits, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Bank deposits (IFS lines 24 and 25); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.OI.02.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.OI.01.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. (Sum(data2025) for three largest banks in Bankscope) / (Sum(data2025) for all banks in Bankscope). Only reported if number of banks in Bankscope is 3 or more. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.OI.06.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. (Sum(data2025) for five largest banks in Bankscope) / (Sum(data2025) for all banks in Bankscope). Only reported if number of banks in Bankscope is 5 or more. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.08.nameEn: Credit to government and state-owned enterprises to GDP (%)
GFDD.EI.08.note: Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. (IFS line 22A + line 22B + line 22C) / GDP. Local currency GDP is from IFS (line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF).
GFDD.EI.08.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.EI.10.nameEn: Bank return on equity (%, before tax)
GFDD.EI.10.note: Raw data are from Bankscope.  Data10270[t] / ((data2055[t] + data2055[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.06.nameEn: Bank return on equity (%, after tax)
GFDD.EI.06.note: Raw data are from Bankscope.  Data2115[t] / ((data2055[t] + data2055[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.09.nameEn: Bank return on assets (%, before tax)
GFDD.EI.09.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. Data10270[t] / ((data2025[t] + data2025[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.05.nameEn: Bank return on assets (%, after tax)
GFDD.EI.05.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. Data2115[t] / ((data2025[t] + data2025[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.04.nameEn: Bank overhead costs to total assets (%)
GFDD.EI.04.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. Data2090[t] / ((data2025[t] + data2025[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.03.nameEn: Bank noninterest income to total income (%)
GFDD.EI.03.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. Data2085 / (data2080 + data2085). Number is only calculated when net-interest income is not negative. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.01.note: Raw data are from Bankscope. Data2080[t] / ((data2010[t] + data2010[t-1])/2). Numerator and denominator are aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.EI.02.note: Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Difference between lending rate and deposit rate. Lending rate is the rate charged by banks on loans to the private sector and deposit interest rate is the rate offered by commercial banks on three-month deposits. IFS line 60P - line 60L.
GFDD.EI.02.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.EI.07.note: Raw data are from Bankscope.  Data2090 / (data2080 + data2085). All Numerator and denominator are first aggregated on the country level before division. Note that banks used in the calculation might differ between indicators. Calculated from underlying bank-by-bank unconsolidated data from Bankscope.

GFDD.DI.01.nameEn: Private credit by deposit money banks to GDP (%)
GFDD.DI.01.note: Private credit by deposit money banks and other financial institutions to GDP, calculated using the following deflation method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is credit to the private sector, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Private credit by deposit money banks (IFS line 22d); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DI.01.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.12.nameEn: Private credit by deposit money banks and other financial institutions to GDP (%)
GFDD.DI.12.note: Private credit by deposit money banks and other financial institutions to GDP, calculated using the following deflation method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is credit to the private sector, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Private credit by deposit money banks and other financial institutions (IFS lines 22d and 42d); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF)
GFDD.DI.12.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.10.nameEn: Non-life insurance premium volume to GDP (%)
GFDD.DI.10.note: Premium data is taken from various issues of Sigma reports (Swiss Re). Data on GDP in US dollars is from the electronic version of the World Development Indicators.

GFDD.DI.07.note: Data taken from a variety of sources such as Investment Company Institute and national sources.
GFDD.DI.07.org: World Bank - Non banking financial database

GFDD.DI.05.note: Ratio of liquid liabilities to GDP, calculated using the following deflation method: {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is liquid liabilities, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF's International Financial Statistics. Liquid liabilities (IFS lines 55L or, if not available, line 35L); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF) For Eurocurrency  area countries liquid liabilities are estimated by summing IFS items 34A, 34B and 35.
GFDD.DI.05.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.09.nameEn: Life insurance premium volume to GDP (%)
GFDD.DI.09.note: Premium data is taken from various issues of Sigma reports (Swiss Re). Data on GDP in US dollars is from the electronic version of the World Development Indicators.

GFDD.DI.11.note: Data taken from a variety of sources such as AXCO and national sources.

GFDD.DI.08.note: Demand, time and saving deposits in deposit money banks and other financial institutions as a share of GDP, calculated using the following deflation method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is demand and time and saving deposits, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Financial system deposits (IFS lines 24, 25, 44, and 45); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DI.08.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.14.nameEn: Domestic credit to private sector (% of GDP)
GFDD.DI.14.note: Domestic credit to private sector refers to financial resources provided to the private sector, such as through loans, purchases of nonequity securities, and trade credits and other accounts receivable, that establish a claim for repayment. For some countries these claims include credit to public enterprises.

GFDD.DI.02.nameEn: Deposit money banks'' assets to GDP (%)
GFDD.DI.02.note: Claims on domestic real nonfinancial sector by deposit money banks as a share of GDP, calculated using the following deflation method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is deposit money bank claims, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF’s International Financial Statistics. Deposit money bank assets (IFS lines 22, a-d); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DI.02.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.04.nameEn: Deposit money bank assets to deposit money bank assets and central bank assets (%)
GFDD.DI.04.note: Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF's International Financial Statistics (IFS lines 12 and 22, a-d).
GFDD.DI.04.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.DI.06.note: Claims on domestic real nonfinancial sector by the Central Bank as a share of GDP, calculated using the following deflation method:  {(0.5)*[Ft/P_et + Ft-1/P_et-1]}/[GDPt/P_at] where F is Central Bank claims, P_e is end-of period CPI, and P_a is average annual CPI. Raw data are from the electronic version of the IMF's International Financial Statistics. Central Bank claims (IFS lines 12, a-d); GDP in local currency (IFS line 99B..ZF or, if not available, line 99B.CZF); end-of period CPI (IFS line 64M..ZF or, if not available, 64Q..ZF); and average annual CPI is calculated using the monthly CPI values (IFS line 64M..ZF).
GFDD.DI.06.org: International Financial Statistics (IFS), International Monetary Fund (IMF)

GFDD.AI.35.note: Proportion of the working capital that was financed by bank loans.

GFDD.AI.31.nameEn: Value of collateral needed for a loan (% of the loan amount)
GFDD.AI.31.note: Value of collateral needed by a formal financial institution for a loan or line of credit as a percentage of the loan value or the value of the line of credit.

GFDD.AI.04.nameEn: Small firms with a bank loan or line of credit (%)
GFDD.AI.04.note: Percentage of small firms (5-19 workers) in the formal sector with a line of credit or a loan from a (formal) financial institution, such as a bank, credit union, microfinance institution, or cooperative.

GFDD.AI.13.nameEn: Saved using a savings club in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.13.note: The percentage of respondents who report saving or setting aside any money by using an informal savings club or a person outside the family in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.13.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.06.nameEn: Saved at a financial institution in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.06.note: The percentage of respondents who report saving or setting aside any money by using an account at a formal financial institution such as a bank, credit union, microfinance institution, or cooperative in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.06.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.12.nameEn: Saved any money in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.12.note: The percentage of respondents who report saving or setting aside any money in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.12.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.24.nameEn: Mobile phone used to send money (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.24.note: The percentage of respondents who report using a mobile phone to send money in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.24.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.23.nameEn: Mobile phone used to pay bills (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.23.note: The percentage of respondents who report using a mobile phone to pay bills in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.23.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.30.note: Percentage of loans where a formal financial institution requires collateral in order to provide the financing.

GFDD.AI.17.nameEn: Loan through store credit in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.17.note: The percentage of respondents who borrowed any money in the past 12 months from a store by using installment credit or buying on credit (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.17.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.14.nameEn: Loan in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.14.note: The percentage of respondents who borrowed any money in the past 12 months from any of the following sources: a formal financial institution, a store by using installment credit, family or friends, employer, or another private lender (% age 15+). (Note that getting a loan does not necessarily require having an account.)
GFDD.AI.14.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.18.nameEn: Loan from family or friends in the past year (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.18.note: The percentage of respondents who report borrowing any money from family or friends in the past 12 months (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.18.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.32.note: Percent of firms that did not apply for a loan in the last fiscal year because they did not need a loan. The denominator is the sum of all firms who applied and did not apply for a loan. The numerator is the number of firms who did not apply for a loan and also stated that they did not need a loan.

GFDD.AI.36.nameEn: Firms identifying access to finance as a major constraint (%)
GFDD.AI.36.note: Percentage of firms identifying access/cost of finance as a "major" or "very severe" obstacle.

GFDD.AI.22.nameEn: Electronic payments used to make payments (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.22.note: The percentage of respondents who used electronic payments (payments that one makes or that are made automatically including wire transfers or payments made online) in the past 12 months to make payments on bills or to buy things using money from their accounts (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.22.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank

GFDD.AI.26.nameEn: Depositing/withdrawing at least once in a typical month (% age 15+)
GFDD.AI.26.note: Adults depositing/withdrawing at least once in a typical month (% age 15+). It is calculated as follows: (100 - "0 deposits/withdrawals in typical month (% with an account,  age 15+)" ) * ("Account at a formal financial institution (% age 15+)") / 100.  "0 deposits/withdrawals in typical month (% with an account,  age 15+)" denotes the percentage of respondents with an account at a formal financial institution who report making zero deposits into or zero withdrawals from their personal account(s) in a typical month (also called “inactive account”). This includes cash or electronic deposits, or any time money is put into or removed from account(s) by self or others (% age 15+, with an account). "Account at a formal financial institution (% age 15+)" denotes the percentage of respondents with an account (self or together with someone else) at a bank, credit union, another financial institution (e.g., cooperative, microfinance institution), or the post office (if applicable) including respondents who reported having a debit card (% age 15+).
GFDD.AI.26.org: Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) Database, World Bank
